spots.name: Bordeaux-Saint-Jean station
spots.summary: Bordeaux-Saint-Jean or formerly Bordeaux-Midi is the main railway station in the French city of Bordeaux. It is the southern terminus of the Paris–Bordeaux railway, and the western terminus of the Chemins de fer du Midi main line from Toulouse.

spots.name: place de la Bourse
spots.summary: The Place de la Bourse is a square in Bordeaux, France, and one of the city's most recognisable sights. Built from 1730 to 1775 along the river Garonne, it was a multi-building development designed by the architect Jacques Gabriel and his son Ange-Jacques Gabriel.

spots.name: Place des Quinconces
spots.summary: The Place des Quinconces, located in Bordeaux, France, is among the largest city squares in Europe.

spots.name: Pont Jacques Chaban-Delmas
spots.summary: The Pont Jacques Chaban-Delmas is a vertical-lift bridge over the Garonne in Bordeaux, France. It was inaugurated on 16 March 2013 by President François Hollande and Alain Juppé, mayor of Bordeaux. Its main span is 110 m (361 ft) long. As of 2013, it is the longest vertical-lift bridge in Europe.

spots.name: Pont de pierre
spots.summary: The Pont de pierre, or "Stone Bridge" in English, is a bridge in Bordeaux,, which connects the left bank of the river Garonne to the right bank quartier de la Bastide.

spots.name: Porte Cailhau
spots.summary: Porte Cailhau is a city gate and triumphal arch located in Bordeaux, France. The five pointed tower is a major fixture of the city's skyline.

spots.name: Palais Rohan, Bordeaux

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Palais Rohan is the Hôtel de Ville, or City Hall, of Bordeaux, France. The building was constructed in the 18th century, originally serving as the Archbishop's Palace of Bordeaux. It was designated a monument historique by the French government in 1997.

spots.name: Rue Sainte-Catherine
spots.summary: The Rue Sainte-Catherine, a 1.2 km long pedestrian street, is the main shopping street in Bordeaux, France.

spots.name: Port de la Lune
spots.summary: The Port de la Lune is the harbour of Bordeaux, France.

spots.name: Grand Théâtre de Bordeaux
spots.summary: The Grand Théâtre de Bordeaux is an opera house in Bordeaux, France, first inaugurated on 17 April 1780. It was in this theatre that the ballet La fille mal gardée premiered in 1789, and where a young Marius Petipa staged some of his first ballets.

spots.name: Musée des Beaux-Arts de Bordeaux

hours.note: Closed Tue

spots.summary: The Musée des Beaux-Arts de Bordeaux is the fine-art museum of the city of Bordeaux, France. The museum is housed in a dependency of the Palais Rohan in central Bordeaux. Its collections include paintings, sculptures and drawings from the 15th century to the 20th century.
